title: Grand epistemic network across two tiers: clustering as an epistemic operation

branches.title: Standard Model history (GEN_HEP v1.2, union of the 12 steps)

stages.title: Witness
stages.what: A witness is tied to what it detects; a task enters.

stages.title: Census
stages.what: Unconnected pairs and uncharted cells are listed.

stages.title: Conjecture
stages.what: An axiom, a model or an open edge is proposed.

stages.title: Refine
stages.what: A distinguished state, a counterexample or a split enters.

stages.title: Possibility
stages.what: Implication, enabling and conversion edges between clusters.

stages.title: No-go
stages.what: Forbidding and separation edges between clusters.

stages.title: Calibrate
stages.what: A measured or simulated value enters as an import.

stages.title: Equivalence
stages.what: Equivalences, specializations and inclusions between clusters.

stages.title: Cluster
stages.what: A generic cluster node enters, or a criterion, test, member or complement edge between generic nodes is added.

stages.title: Descend
stages.what: An inclusion between generic clusters is carried down to a generic distinguished state.

stages.title: Cluster ↑
stages.what: An abstraction edge joins a node of a named system and a generic node: the system node is a member of a generic cluster or is cut by it, a system observable is a test of a generic cluster, or a generic cluster is a subset of a state space of the readers (its carrier).

stages.title: Descend ↓
stages.what: The membership of a node of a named system in a generic cluster is derived from an inclusion between clusters, or is observed through a witness.

stages.title: Observe
stages.what: A direct observable of a named system enters.

stages.title: Deficit
stages.what: An observable has no route from the model layer.

stages.title: Hypothesize
stages.what: A law, a term or a frame is added or rewritten.

stages.title: Restructure
stages.what: State nodes are added, extended, split, composed; routes enter model nodes.

stages.title: Predict
stages.what: A route from model and state to an observable or a state.

stages.title: Falsify
stages.what: A derivation fails against the observable.

stages.title: Calibrate
stages.what: An observable fixes a parameter.

stages.title: Reduce
stages.what: Models are merged, absorbed or reduced.

stages.title: Cluster
stages.what: Nodes of a named system are clustered inside the system: symmetry classes, sectors and groups of sectors, families of observables, clusters of terms.

stages.title: Descend
stages.what: An inclusion between clusters of a named system is carried down to a member.

operations.counts: +1 node (+2 with the complement), +1 criterion edge, +|U| member edges
operations.text: Add a cluster node c for the set U of nodes of one layer that satisfy a predicate supplied by the model-layer node f.
Attach an observable-layer functional w that decides, completely or in part, whether an object is in c.
Add a node that is a sum, a direct sum or a moment of its members (total energy, Fock ladder, first moment of a distribution).
From routes between members of a and members of b, or from an implication of the incidence table, propose an edge between the clusters.

operations.sig: (a subset b), u in a -> u in b
operations.text: Carry an inclusion between clusters down to a member; with a witness and data, the membership has status observed.
Split a cluster, add a counterexample atom, or restrict an inclusion to a frame, when a derived fact contradicts a stated one or an implication is refuted.
An observable-layer cluster (a table of outcome statistics, a set of measurements) is taken as the object of a resource theory and placed in its state layer.

rules.name: Symmetry partition
rules.text: A symmetry represented on the state layer partitions it; the labels of the pieces become observables.

rules.name: In-degree-zero drive
rules.text: An observable with no route from the model layer drives a change of the model layer.

rules.name: Fock extension
rules.text: A field node extends each realized class to a sector with an occupation ladder.

rules.name: Route composition
rules.text: An interaction term is entered by an AND route with one leg per field of the term.

rules.name: Effective status
rules.text: A term whose coupling has negative mass dimension is marked effective from the moment it is added.

rules.name: Universality merge
rules.text: Model nodes that share one calibration are merged.

rules.name: Absorption
rules.text: An effective node is absorbed into a fundamental one; the mediator sector enters every former route.

rules.name: Sector refinement
rules.text: A state node is split or replaced only through an observable or a model back-edge.

rules.name: Calibration
rules.text: One parameter is fixed by one observable; the remaining edges of the node are predictions.

rules.name: Clustering of models
rules.text: Model nodes are grouped inside the term they belong to, with lineage edges.

rules.name: Derivation
rules.text: A node is derived by an AND route from nodes already present (no forward links).

rules.name: Failed route
rules.text: A derivation that contradicts the observable is kept as a failed route and resolved by a later node.

rules.name: Census
rules.text: Every unconnected pair or uncharted cell is listed as an open item.

rules.name: Closure
rules.text: An open item is closed by composition, by an elementary computation, by a counterexample or from the literature.

rules.name: Composition
rules.text: Independent new observables are composed as tensor-product sectors.

rules.name: Reduction
rules.text: A model is reduced to its simplest representation (parameter ties, commutant decomposition, equivalences).

rules.name: State clustering
rules.text: Guard: a model-layer node f supplies a predicate that separates state nodes (an invariance, a subtheory, a partition, a constraint), or routes into one target differ only by one leg. Action: add the cluster node, its complement where a carrier is fixed, the criterion edge from f and the member edges. R1 is the case of an invariance inside one system.

rules.name: Observable clustering
rules.text: Three forms. Family: observables of one process type are members of a family node. Aggregate: a node is a sum or a moment of its members. Effect: given a reference model m0 and a functional w that m0 bounds, the effect is the set of observable data outside the bound, with a no-go edge from m0, the test edge from w and the member edges. The effect is the deficit of rule R2 against a model that is kept fixed.

rules.name: Lift
rules.text: Guard: two clusters with members and no edge between them, and either a member-level route from one into the other or an implication of the incidence table. Action: add the edge with status open; it is closed by R14.

rules.name: Descent
rules.text: Guard: an inclusion a ⊆ b with status theorem or definition, a member u of a, u an object of the kind on which b is defined, and the frame of the inclusion holds for u. Action: add the member edge u ∈ b with status derived and the excluded edge for the complement. With a witness of b and measured data of u the status is observed.

rules.name: Refinement
rules.text: Guard: a derived fact contradicts a stated one, or an implication of the incidence table is refuted by an object. Action: split the cluster, add the counterexample as an atom, or restrict the inclusion to a frame.

nodes.label: Force on a charge
nodes.desc: Measured from a body's acceleration (F = ma) or by balancing it against a known force. Every force law in the story predicts it, so more and more alternative routes lead here.

nodes.label: Position
nodes.desc: Where a body sits in Euclidean 3-space, measured with rulers. Separations r = x − x′ enter every force law. A primitive geometric observable.

nodes.label: Velocity
nodes.desc: v = dx/dt from successive position measurements. It becomes essential once magnetic forces turn out to depend on motion.

nodes.label: Particle state of motion
nodes.desc: Position and velocity together: Newton's description of a body's state.

nodes.label: Vector addition
nodes.desc: How forces and fields combine. Because order and grouping do not matter, the total force from any number of sources is well defined.

nodes.label: Time derivative
nodes.desc: Generates time evolution. Its commuting with spatial derivatives is used when the curl equations are combined into wave equations.

nodes.label: Electric charge
nodes.desc: A signed scalar property of bodies, inferred from the forces they exert on one another. Experimentally additive and conserved, and (Millikan) quantized in units of e.

nodes.label: Additivity and conservation of charge
nodes.desc: Franklin's principle: charges add with sign, and electrification only moves charge from one body to another. A global statement that the continuity equation later makes local.

nodes.label: Coulomb law
nodes.desc: k q₁q₂ r̂/r² with k = 1/4πε₀. Exchange symmetry gives Newton's third law; the inverse-square form is exactly what makes Gauss's law hold.

nodes.label: Point-charge configuration
nodes.desc: The simplest state of an electrostatic system: which charges there are and where they sit.

nodes.label: Superposition
nodes.desc: The map from sources to forces and fields is linear: contributions from separate sources simply add. Exact in vacuum Maxwell theory.

nodes.label: Poisson's equation
nodes.desc: ∇²φ = −ρ/ε₀. Linearity means solutions superpose; uniqueness means sources plus boundary data fully determine the state.

nodes.label: Charge density
nodes.desc: Charge per unit volume. Smooth densities and point charges (via δ functions) are elements of the same space.

nodes.label: Delta function
nodes.desc: Lets point charges and smooth densities live in one space: ρ = Σ qᵢ δ³(x − xᵢ). Introduced by Dirac (1927) and made rigorous by Schwartz (1945).

nodes.label: Potential up to a constant
nodes.desc: The electrostatic state written as one scalar function, with its built-in redundancy made explicit.

nodes.label: Boundary values
nodes.desc: The part of the state fixed by conductors and the outside world. Needed to make Poisson's problem well posed.

nodes.label: Gradient
nodes.desc: Because ∇ kills constants, φ and φ + c give the same force. This is the first redundancy (gauge freedom) in the description of the state.

nodes.label: Divergence theorem
nodes.desc: Converts local statements about sources into statements about flux through surfaces, and back. Also used for any flux integral.

nodes.label: Electric flux
nodes.desc: Φ_E = ∮E·dA through a closed surface. Gauss's law says it equals Q_enc/ε₀ however the enclosed charges are arranged.

nodes.label: Symmetry arguments
nodes.desc: If a source distribution is unchanged by rotations, translations or reflections, the field it produces must transform the same way. With Gauss's or Ampère's law this fixes fields without integrating.

nodes.label: Electric field value
nodes.desc: Operationally E = lim F/q for a small test charge at rest: a derived observable built from force and charge measurements.

nodes.label: Electric field
nodes.desc: The whole field as one object, a function on space. A calculating device for Green and Gauss; a physical state for Faraday and Maxwell.

nodes.label: Line integrals
nodes.desc: Integrals along curves. Path independence holds for curl-free fields on regions without holes; the exception returns with holonomy in the final section.

nodes.label: Electrostatic energy
nodes.desc: Work needed to assemble a configuration from charges far apart. Measured through work done or heat released on discharge.

nodes.label: Quadratic energy form
nodes.desc: U(E₁ + E₂) = U(E₁) + U(E₂) + a cross term. The cross term is why energies do not simply add even though fields do.

nodes.label: Voltage
nodes.desc: Volta's tension, a potential difference φ(b) − φ(a): what a voltmeter reads. Invariant under φ → φ + const, which is why it is measurable while φ itself is not.

nodes.label: Capacitance
nodes.desc: C = Q/ΔV for a conductor or pair of conductors. Depends only on geometry (and the medium) because electrostatics is linear.

nodes.label: Current
nodes.desc: I = dQ/dt through a surface, read by an ammeter. Equal to the flux of the current density.

nodes.label: Current density
nodes.desc: Charge flux per unit area. Together with ρ it specifies all the sources of the field.

nodes.label: Resistance
nodes.desc: R = ΔV/I for a conductor. Ohm found it independent of the current for a given wire at fixed temperature.

nodes.label: Ohm's law
nodes.desc: J = σE inside a conductor, or ΔV = IR for a whole wire. Unlike Maxwell's equations it describes a material, valid for many conductors at moderate fields.

nodes.label: Continuity equation
nodes.desc: Charge cannot vanish in one place and reappear in another: change inside a volume equals flux through its boundary. Later developments derive it rather than assume it.

nodes.label: Magnetic field value
nodes.desc: The magnetic action at a point, read with a compass or a probe coil, or inferred from the velocity-dependent force on a moving charge.

nodes.label: Biot–Savart law
nodes.desc: Field of a current element, (μ₀/4π) I dl × r̂/r². The magnetic counterpart of the Coulomb law.

nodes.label: Cross product
nodes.desc: a×b = −b×a, and a×(b×c) ≠ (a×b)×c. Its dependence on handedness makes B a pseudovector, and since v×B ⟂ v, magnetic forces do no work.

nodes.label: Curl and Stokes' theorem
nodes.desc: Measures circulation. The identity div∘curl = 0 is what later forces the displacement current.

nodes.label: Magnetic field
nodes.desc: The magnetic field as a single object on space.

nodes.label: Electromotive force
nodes.desc: ℰ = ∮(E + v×B)·dl around a circuit, measured as the voltage across a small gap in the loop.

nodes.label: Magnetic flux
nodes.desc: Φ_B = ∫B·dA through a surface bounded by a loop: Faraday's count of lines of force threading a circuit.

nodes.label: Faraday's law
nodes.desc: A changing magnetic flux induces a circulating electric field; the minus sign makes induced currents oppose the change.

nodes.label: Vector potential
nodes.desc: Neumann's and Thomson's potential, Maxwell's electromagnetic momentum. Useful for calculation; not observable by itself.

nodes.label: Couplings ε₀ and μ₀
nodes.desc: Fix the strength of electric forces between charges and magnetic forces between currents. 1/√(ε₀μ₀) is the speed Weber and Kohlrausch found as a ratio of units. (In the 2019 SI they are fixed through the measured fine-structure constant.)

nodes.label: Speed of light
nodes.desc: Measured astronomically (Rømer 1676, Bradley 1729) and on Earth by Fizeau (1849). After Maxwell it is also predicted from ε₀ and μ₀. Only the prediction is drawn as a route; the measurements are not.

nodes.label: Maxwell's equations
nodes.desc: The complete field law. Gauss's two laws constrain each moment; Faraday's and the Ampère–Maxwell law evolve it.

nodes.label: Dynamical field state
nodes.desc: Electric and magnetic fields as one state that evolves in time.

nodes.label: Field energy density
nodes.desc: u = ½(ε₀|E|² + |B|²/μ₀). Integrates to the total energy stored in the field.

nodes.label: Maxwell stress tensor
nodes.desc: Expresses the force on charges inside a volume as a surface integral over the field around them.

nodes.label: Wave operator
nodes.desc: □ = c⁻²∂²/∂t² − ∇². Choosing the retarded Green's function means influences travel at c from the past.

nodes.label: Gauge fixing
nodes.desc: A rule that picks one pair (φ, A) from each class, chosen to simplify the equations.

nodes.label: Gauge transformations
nodes.desc: (φ, A) → (φ − ∂χ/∂t, A + ∇χ). Two transformations compose in either order to χ₁ + χ₂: the group is commutative.

nodes.label: Gauge class of potentials
nodes.desc: The physical state in the potential description. Everything observable is a function of these classes.

nodes.label: Poincaré lemma
nodes.desc: ∇·B = 0 ⇒ B = ∇×A, and ∇×(E + ∂A/∂t) = 0 ⇒ E + ∂A/∂t = −∇φ. It can fail on regions with holes, which is where holonomy lives.

nodes.label: Poynting's theorem
nodes.desc: ∂u/∂t + ∇·S = −J·E: field energy changes by flowing away or by doing work on charges.

nodes.label: Poynting vector
nodes.desc: S = E×B/μ₀, the energy flux in W/m². Its time average is the intensity a detector measures.

nodes.label: Wave data
nodes.desc: Wavelength, frequency and polarization, measured with standing waves, interferometers and polarizers. In vacuum ω = c|k| and k ⟂ E ⟂ B.

nodes.label: Radiation modes
nodes.desc: The source-free field described by its modes rather than by its values at points.

nodes.label: Fourier decomposition
nodes.desc: Writes any field as a superposition of plane waves e^{i(k·x − ωt)}, in which the field equations become algebraic.

nodes.label: Field momentum density
nodes.desc: g = S/c². Observed as radiation pressure on mirrors and absorbers.

nodes.label: Radiated power
nodes.desc: Energy per unit time leaving an accelerating charge through a distant sphere.

nodes.label: Lorentz group
nodes.desc: Two non-parallel boosts compose to a boost plus a rotation (the Wigner rotation). Under boosts, E and B mix.

nodes.label: Four-potential
nodes.desc: Scalar and vector potentials as a single spacetime object.

nodes.label: Four-current
nodes.desc: Charge and current density as a single spacetime object.

nodes.label: Field tensor
nodes.desc: Electric and magnetic fields as one observer-independent object.

nodes.label: Lorentz invariants
nodes.desc: E·B and |E|² − c²|B|² take the same value for every inertial observer. If E ⟂ B and |E| < c|B|, some frame sees a purely magnetic field.

nodes.label: Energy–momentum tensor
nodes.desc: One symmetric tensor whose components, for a given observer, are the energy density, Poynting flux, momentum density and Maxwell stress.

nodes.label: Action principle
nodes.desc: Under a gauge change L shifts by q dχ/dt, a total time derivative, so the equations of motion are unchanged.

nodes.label: Legendre transform
nodes.desc: Moves from the velocity description to the momentum description: p = ∂L/∂v, H = p·v − L.

nodes.label: Particle phase space
nodes.desc: The Hamiltonian state of a charge. Using kinetic momenta as coordinates instead puts the magnetic field into the symplectic form.

nodes.label: Kinetic momentum
nodes.desc: π = mv = p − qA. Gauge-invariant and measurable, for example from the curvature of a particle track. The canonical momentum p is not.

nodes.label: Poisson bracket
nodes.desc: dF/dt = {F, H}. In a magnetic field the kinetic momenta do not commute: a classical non-commutativity that becomes Landau levels in quantum mechanics.

nodes.label: Field phase space
nodes.desc: The field as a constrained Hamiltonian system. Gauss's law generates the gauge transformations.

nodes.label: Noether's theorem
nodes.desc: Every continuous symmetry of the action yields a conservation law.

nodes.label: Conserved totals
nodes.desc: Total energy, momentum and angular momentum of matter plus field. Conservation holds only when the field's contributions are included.

nodes.label: Exterior derivative
nodes.desc: Unifies grad, curl and div. d² = 0 contains both curl∘grad = 0 and div∘curl = 0.

nodes.label: Wedge product
nodes.desc: α∧β = (−1)^{pq} β∧α: 1-forms anticommute, 2-forms commute. F∧F is a 4-form proportional to E·B.

nodes.label: Hodge star
nodes.desc: Carries all metric (and constitutive) information. In form language it is the only place c and spacetime geometry enter Maxwell's equations.

nodes.label: U(1) bundle
nodes.desc: The global geometric state. It can carry information, such as holonomy around holes, that no single local potential captures.

nodes.label: U(1) connection
nodes.desc: In a non-abelian (Yang–Mills) theory the curvature is dA + A∧A. Electromagnetism's commutative group keeps it linear.

nodes.label: Holonomy
nodes.desc: ∮A·dl around a closed loop: gauge-invariant and equal to the enclosed flux. Around a solenoid it is non-zero on loops where B = 0. With ħ, the phase exp(iq∮A·dl/ħ) is the Aharonov–Bohm phase.

nodes.label: Blackbody spectrum
nodes.desc: Energy density of cavity radiation per unit frequency at temperature T, measured with bolometers around 1900. It has a peak and falls at high frequency, which classical physics cannot reproduce.

nodes.label: Equipartition theorem
nodes.desc: Classical statistical mechanics gives every oscillator mean energy kT. Applied to infinitely many radiation modes, it gives infinite energy.

nodes.label: Planck relation
nodes.desc: The first quantum rule. It ties a frequency, a wave property, to an energy, a particle property.

nodes.label: Planck's constant
nodes.desc: h ≈ 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, with ħ = h/2π. The quantum of action; classical physics is the regime where actions are large compared with ħ. Exact by definition in the 2019 SI.

nodes.label: Photoelectric effect
nodes.desc: Maximum kinetic energy of electrons ejected by light. It rises linearly with frequency above a threshold and does not depend on intensity.

nodes.label: Photon
nodes.desc: A quantum of the electromagnetic field, with energy ħω and momentum ħk. Detected one at a time by photomultipliers and in Compton scattering.

nodes.label: Spectral lines
nodes.desc: Sharp wavelengths emitted or absorbed by atoms. Hydrogen's lines fit 1/λ = R(1/m² − 1/n²).

nodes.label: Bohr orbits
nodes.desc: The old quantum theory's hybrid state: classical orbits with quantum selection rules. Superseded by quantum mechanics but historically the bridge.

nodes.label: Canonical commutator
nodes.desc: Shares every algebraic property of the Poisson bracket, which is why Dirac could map one to the other. Its non-zero value iħ is the quantum.

nodes.label: Operator algebra
nodes.desc: Observables become operators on states. Position and momentum no longer commute, so they cannot both be sharp: Heisenberg's uncertainty relation.

nodes.label: Schrödinger equation
nodes.desc: iħ ∂ψ/∂t = Ĥψ. Linearity means quantum states superpose, the quantum descendant of the superposition principle of Part I.

nodes.label: Hilbert-space state
nodes.desc: Replaces the point in phase space. It assigns amplitudes, not definite values, to every observable.

nodes.label: Born rule
nodes.desc: Connects the abstract state to what detectors record: frequencies of outcomes over many runs.

nodes.label: Outcome statistics
nodes.desc: Probabilities and averages of measurement results over many identically prepared systems.

nodes.label: Minimal coupling
nodes.desc: The quantum version of the classical kinetic momentum. It makes the potentials, not only the fields, act on charged quantum particles.

nodes.label: Landau levels
nodes.desc: Discrete energies of a charge in a uniform magnetic field, seen in cyclotron resonance and the quantum Hall effect.

nodes.label: Aharonov–Bohm shift
nodes.desc: Shift of an interference pattern by qΦ_B/ħ for electrons passing around a region of magnetic flux they never enter.

nodes.label: Clifford algebra
nodes.desc: The algebra needed to take a square root of p² − m²c². Its anticommutation, not commutation, is what produces spin ½.

nodes.label: Dirac equation
nodes.desc: The relativistic wave equation of the electron, the matter half of QED.

nodes.label: Dirac spinor
nodes.desc: A spinor changes sign under a full 360° rotation, something no classical vector field does.

nodes.label: Electron g-factor
nodes.desc: Ratio of the electron's magnetic moment to its spin in natural units. Dirac predicted exactly 2.

nodes.label: Positron
nodes.desc: The electron's antiparticle, same mass, opposite charge. Electron–positron pairs are created and annihilated.

nodes.label: Creation and annihilation operators
nodes.desc: Quantizing each field mode as an oscillator. Commutators give bosons (photons); anticommutators give fermions (electrons).

nodes.label: Fock space
nodes.desc: The state space of a quantum field, in which particle number can change.

nodes.label: Field operator
nodes.desc: The quantized electromagnetic potential. Its expectation values in coherent states are classical fields.

nodes.label: Spontaneous emission rate
nodes.desc: Rate at which an excited atom emits a photon with no field present, set by vacuum fluctuations.

nodes.label: Casimir force
nodes.desc: Attraction between uncharged parallel plates due to the change in zero-point energy of the field modes between them.

nodes.label: Electron–positron field
nodes.desc: The electron as the quantum of a field. It annihilates electrons and creates positrons.

nodes.label: Fine-structure constant
nodes.desc: α = e²/4πε₀ħc ≈ 1/137.036, the dimensionless strength of electromagnetism. Measured from the electron's g-factor and from atom-recoil experiments.

nodes.label: Perturbation series
nodes.desc: Expands amplitudes in powers of the small coupling α. Each higher order involves more virtual particles.

nodes.label: Lamb shift
nodes.desc: Splitting between hydrogen's 2S½ and 2P½ levels: about 1000 MHz in Lamb and Retherford's 1947 measurement, about 1058 MHz in later, more precise measurements.

nodes.label: Anomalous magnetic moment
nodes.desc: a_e = (g − 2)/2 ≈ 0.00115965, measured by Kusch and Foley (1947) and today to about a tenth of a part per billion.

nodes.label: Renormalization
nodes.desc: Expresses predictions in terms of measured quantities, so that infinities cancel. Later understood through the renormalization group.

nodes.label: Path integral
nodes.desc: Quantizes using the classical action directly, so the action principle of Part I becomes the core of quantum theory.

nodes.label: Feynman diagrams
nodes.desc: Pictorial rules for the terms of the perturbation series.

nodes.label: S-matrix
nodes.desc: Packages everything that can be measured in a scattering experiment.

nodes.label: Cross sections
nodes.desc: Scattering rates per unit flux, measured in collision experiments (Compton, Møller, Bhabha scattering).

nodes.label: Running coupling
nodes.desc: The effective strength of electromagnetism at momentum transfer Q, measured at colliders: about 1/128 at the Z mass.

nodes.label: Local gauge principle
nodes.desc: Demanding local phase invariance requires a connection, the electromagnetic potential, and fixes how it couples to charge.

nodes.label: QED Lagrangian
nodes.desc: The complete specification of quantum electrodynamics in one line: Dirac field plus Maxwell field, coupled through the covariant derivative.

nodes.label: Ward–Takahashi identities
nodes.desc: Relations among amplitudes implied by gauge symmetry; they protect the theory's consistency through renormalization.

nodes.label: H_{1} — one-particle Hilbert space
nodes.desc: A state is a ray in a separable Hilbert space H_{1}. The space describes exactly one particle: there is no operator in the one-particle framework whose eigenvalue is a particle number.

nodes.label: Particle Lagrangian L = ½mẋ^{2} − V(x)
nodes.desc: The one-particle Lagrangian fixes the Hamiltonian and therefore both the evolution U(t) and the energy spectrum (e.g. E_{n} = −13.6 eV/n^{2} for hydrogen). Replaced by relativistic wave equations at Step 2 and by the free-field Lagrangian at Step 4.

nodes.label: Unitary evolution U(t) = e^{−iĤt/ħ}
nodes.desc: Time evolution is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group generated by the Hamiltonian (Stone 1932). It maps H_{1} onto H_{1}: the back-edge to the state layer. Particle number is conserved by construction.

nodes.label: Observable postulate: Â = Â^{†}, Born rule
nodes.desc: Every self-adjoint operator on H_{1} is an observable; its spectrum lists the possible outcomes and the Born rule gives their probabilities (von Neumann 1932). This node sends one edge to each Hermitian operator in the observable layer.

nodes.label: Energy levels (spectrum of Ĥ)
nodes.desc: The discrete spectra observed since Balmer (1885) are the eigenvalues of Ĥ; Schrödinger (1926) derived the hydrogen levels. Dirac (1928) adds the fine structure. Observed first, explained later: anomaly-driven.

nodes.label: Spin Ŝ_{z} = ±ħ/2
nodes.desc: Spin was observed (Stern–Gerlach 1922) and postulated (Uhlenbeck & Goudsmit 1925) before Pauli (1927) and Dirac (1928) gave it a place in the formalism: anomaly-driven.

nodes.label: Mass m (Casimir P^{μ}P_{μ} = m^{2})
nodes.desc: In the Poincaré-covariant theory mass is the eigenvalue of the Casimir operator P^{2}; it labels the representation rather than being a dynamical variable.

nodes.label: Spin s / helicity h (Casimir W^{μ}W_{μ})
nodes.desc: The Pauli–Lubański Casimir gives spin for m > 0; for m = 0 the invariant is the helicity. Both are representation labels.

nodes.label: Particle production and decay
nodes.desc: (i) Emission and absorption of light, Einstein A and B coefficients (1917). (ii) β decay with a continuous electron spectrum (Chadwick 1914; Ellis & Wooster 1927); the electron is not a nuclear constituent. (iii) e^{+}e^{−} pairs created by γ rays (Anderson 1…

nodes.label: e^{−}
nodes.desc: Fock sector built on the electron UIR. The Dirac field ψ_{e} annihilates e^{−} and creates e^{+}, so the N-particle nodes count electrons and positrons together.

nodes.label: p
nodes.desc: Proton sector (Rutherford 1919). Treated as elementary in Fermi's theory; replaced by quark sectors at Step 9 (the proton is a bound state of the strong sector, which is outside this graph).

nodes.label: n
nodes.desc: Neutron sector (Chadwick 1932). Replaced by quark sectors at Step 9.

nodes.label: ν
nodes.desc: Neutrino sector as assumed from Pauli (1930) to 1962: a single massless species. Detected by Cowan & Reines (1956). Split into ν_{e} and ν_{μ} at Step 7.

nodes.label: γ
nodes.desc: Photon sector: the quantized radiation field A_{μ} of Dirac (1927). Bosonic ladder: symmetrized N-photon states.

nodes.label: Quantum field on Fock space (a, a^{†})
nodes.desc: The field is the operator that adds or removes one quantum of a given UIR. The Fock space of a species is ⊕_{N} Sym^{N}H_{1} (bosons) or ⊕_{N} Λ^{N}H_{1} (fermions) (Fock 1932); spin–statistics proved by Fierz (1939) and Pauli (1940). The free Lagrangian L_{0…

nodes.label: Decay width Γ (lifetime τ = ħ/Γ)
nodes.desc: The generic transition-rate observable. Dirac (1927) derived the rate formula later called Fermi's golden rule. Without an interaction term the rate is zero, so this family stays unexplained until Step 5.

nodes.label: Cross section σ, dσ/dΩ
nodes.desc: The generic scattering observable, defined through S-matrix elements (Wheeler 1937; Heisenberg 1943; Dyson 1949). S = 1 for the free field.

nodes.label: QED vertex −e ψ̄γ^{μ}ψ A_{μ}
nodes.desc: Minimal coupling p → p − eA applied to the quantized fields gives the single interaction term −e ψ̄γ^{μ}ψA_{μ}. One vertex changes N_{γ} by ±1 and N_{e} by 0 (scattering) or ±2 (pair creation/annihilation). Renormalized to all orders by Tomonaga, Schwinger, F…

nodes.label: Compton scattering dσ/dΩ
nodes.desc: Compton (1923) measured the wavelength shift and intensity; the Klein–Nishina formula (1929), the first QED cross section from the Dirac equation, reproduces the angular distribution and the high-energy fall-off.

nodes.label: e^{+}e^{−} pair production σ(γ → e^{+}e^{−})
nodes.desc: Dirac's hole theory (1930–31) implied an anti-electron; Anderson (1933) and Blackett & Occhialini (1933) observed it. The Bethe–Heitler cross section (1934) in the field of a nucleus follows from the QED vertex at order α^{3}.

nodes.label: Electron anomaly a_{e} = (g−2)/2
nodes.desc: Kusch & Foley (1948) found g = 2(1.00119 ± 0.00005). Schwinger (1948) computed the one-loop value α/2π. Today a_{e} is known to ~10^{−13} and agrees with the five-loop QED calculation (PDG).

nodes.label: Lamb shift 2S_{1/2} − 2P_{1/2}
nodes.desc: Lamb & Retherford (1947) measured a splitting of about 1000 MHz that the Dirac equation sets to zero; Bethe (1947) obtained ≈1040 MHz from the electron self-energy with a nonrelativistic cut-off. The modern value is 1057.8 MHz.

nodes.label: Fine-structure constant α ≈ 1/137.036
nodes.desc: The coupling in the QED vertex is not predicted; α is measured (today most precisely from a_{e} and atom-recoil experiments) and fixes e. Calibration edge.

nodes.label: β-decay rate and spectrum shape
nodes.desc: Chadwick (1914) found the β spectrum continuous; Ellis & Wooster (1927) showed the energy is really missing. Fermi's node gives the rate and the shape (Kurie et al. 1936) from phase space × |M|^{2}.

nodes.label: Fermi contact term G_{F}(p̄γ^{μ}n)(ēγ_{μ}ν)

nodes.label: Neutron lifetime τ_{n} ≈ 878 s
nodes.desc: Free-neutron decay n → p e ν̄ was expected once m_{n} > m_{p} + m_{e} was established (Chadwick & Goldhaber 1935) and first measured by Robson (1951). Current value 878.4 ± 0.5 s (PDG 2024).

nodes.desc: The strength of the contact term is an input. From Step 9 on it is a derived combination g^{2}/(4√2 M_{W}^{2}), but still fixed by measurement (τ_{μ}).

nodes.label: ν_{e}
nodes.desc: Electron-neutrino sector. In the SM as drawn it is massless and left-handed only (no right-handed state), which is what blocks a mass term at Step 11.

nodes.label: μ
nodes.desc: Muon sector (Neddermeyer & Anderson 1937). Shown not to be Yukawa's strongly interacting meson by Conversi, Pancini & Piccioni (1947).

nodes.label: ν_{μ}
nodes.desc: Muon-neutrino sector, distinguished from ν_{e} by Danby et al. (1962): neutrinos from π→μν produce μ, not e.

nodes.desc: The muon itself was unexpected (1937). Its lifetime, ~2.2 μs, is reproduced by the contact node with the β-decay value of G_{F}: the universality signal.

nodes.label: Michel spectrum, ρ = ¾
nodes.desc: Michel (1950) parametrized the electron spectrum of μ decay by ρ; the measured ρ = 0.7518 ± 0.0026 (PDG) agrees with the V−A value ¾.

nodes.label: Neutrino helicity h(ν) = −1

nodes.label: u
nodes.desc: Up-quark sector (Gell-Mann 1964; Zweig 1964; point-like constituents seen in deep inelastic scattering, SLAC 1969). Colour and the gluon sector are not drawn.

nodes.label: d
nodes.desc: Down-quark sector. In the charged current it enters as the Cabibbo-rotated combination d' = cos θ_{C} d + sin θ_{C} s (Cabibbo 1963).

nodes.label: W^{±}
nodes.desc: Charged weak boson sector, M_{W} ≈ 80.4 GeV. First observed at the CERN SPS collider (UA1, UA2, 1983).

nodes.label: Z^{0}
nodes.desc: Neutral weak boson sector, M_{Z} ≈ 91.19 GeV (UA1/UA2 1983; LEP precision 1989–2000).

nodes.label: Neutral-current events, R_{ν} = σ(NC)/σ(CC)

nodes.desc: Predicted from G_{F}, α and sin^{2}θ_{W}: M_{W}^{2} = πα/(√2 G_{F} sin^{2}θ_{W}) at tree level (≈78 GeV), ≈80.4 GeV with radiative corrections. Observed at the SPS in 1983. PDG 2024 average 80.369 ± 0.013 GeV (CDF 2022 value excluded from the average).

nodes.desc: Tree-level relation M_{Z} = M_{W}/cos θ_{W}; observed in 1983 (UA1, UA2) and measured to 2 MeV at LEP.

nodes.label: Weak mixing angle sin^{2}θ_{W} ≈ 0.23
nodes.desc: The one new parameter of the neutral current. Calibration edge: measured, not predicted.

nodes.label: Z width → N_{ν} = 2.984 ± 0.008
nodes.desc: The Z line shape gives the invisible width, i.e. the number of light neutrino sectors coupling to the Z: 2.9840 ± 0.0082 (LEP EWWG 2006). A model-layer prediction about the number of state-layer sectors.

nodes.label: σ(e^{+}e^{−} → W^{+}W^{−}) and triple-gauge couplings

nodes.label: H
nodes.desc: Higgs-boson sector, m_{H} ≈ 125 GeV (ATLAS, CMS 2012). The scalar doublet Φ has one physical excitation after three components are absorbed by W^{±}, Z.

nodes.label: Higgs potential V = −μ^{2}Φ^{†}Φ + λ(Φ^{†}Φ)^{2} → m_{H}^{2} = 2λv^{2}
nodes.desc: The potential fixes v^{2} = μ^{2}/λ and the physical scalar mass m_{H}^{2} = 2λv^{2}. The measured m_{H} fixes λ ≈ 0.13 (calibration); the trilinear coupling λ_{HHH} is then predicted but not yet measured, only bounded by di-Higgs searches.

nodes.label: Higgs mass m_{H} = 125.2 GeV
nodes.desc: Existence predicted in 1964; discovered 2012. The value is an input that fixes λ = m_{H}^{2}/2v^{2} ≈ 0.13 (PDG 2024: 125.20 ± 0.11 GeV).

nodes.label: Higgs rates σ×BR: γγ, ZZ^{*}, WW^{*}, ττ, bb̄
nodes.desc: Production (gluon fusion, vector-boson fusion, VH) and decay rates relative to the SM expectation; all measured signal strengths are consistent with 1 within uncertainties (PDG 2024 review).

nodes.label: Fermion masses m_{e}, m_{μ}, m_{u}, m_{d}
nodes.desc: The SM explains the mechanism of fermion mass but not the values: each mass fixes one Yukawa coupling. Calibration edges.

nodes.label: Higgs self-coupling λ_{HHH}
nodes.desc: Di-Higgs production has not been observed; current limits constrain λ_{HHH}/λ_{SM} to roughly a window of order unity around the SM value (ATLAS/CMS, Run 2). A prediction awaiting its observable.

nodes.desc: One term of the SM Lagrangian, written with the covariant derivative of SU(2)_{L}×U(1)_{Y}. Expanding D_{μ} gives exactly three vertex types: the electromagnetic vertex (Step 5), the charged current (Step 9) and the neutral current (Step 9). The three effecti…

nodes.label: Gauge kinetic term −¼W^{a}_{μν}W^{aμν} − ¼B_{μν}B^{μν}
nodes.desc: The Yang–Mills field strength contains the cubic and quartic self-couplings of the W and Z. No effective node was ever written for these vertices; they were predicted and then tested (LEP2).

nodes.desc: The gauge-covariant kinetic term of the scalar doublet. With ⟨Φ⟩ = v/√2 it produces the W and Z masses and the Higgs–gauge vertices.

nodes.label: Yukawa term −y_{f} f̄_{L}Φ f_{R} + h.c.
nodes.desc: The only SM term that distinguishes the fermion generations; its couplings are inputs (calibration edges).

nodes.desc: Fixes the vacuum value and the Higgs mass; the self-couplings it predicts are the least tested part of the model.

nodes.label: Beyond the SM: candidate ν-mass term
nodes.desc: Holds the candidate repairs for the neutrino-oscillation observable. It is drawn dashed because none of its members is established.

nodes.label: Symplectic / Poisson structure
nodes.desc: Classical kinematics: phase space (M, omega), observables = real functions, Poisson bracket {f,g}, Liouville flow. The common substrate of every model in the genesis column.

nodes.label: Epistemic restriction
nodes.desc: Classical statistical theory restricted to knowledge-balanced (uncertainty-saturating) distributions; cell area set by hbar. Generates the whole noncontextual-but-nonclassical shell.

nodes.label: Poisson-to-commutator lift (Moyal)
nodes.desc: Deformation of the observable algebra: star product; Moyal bracket = Poisson bracket + sum of hbar^2k higher-derivative terms; [f,g]_star = i hbar {f,g}_Moyal. Groenewold - van Hove: no exact Poisson-to-commutator morphism beyond quadratics.

nodes.label: Complex structure (i)
nodes.desc: Amplitudes in C: i[A,B] is again an observable, so observables form a Lie algebra and coincide with generators (Stone). Carries local tomography and imaginarity.

nodes.label: hbar as deformation scale
nodes.desc: Sets the epistemic cell area and the deformation parameter of the Moyal lift; hbar to 0 contracts Moyal to Poisson, quantum to classical simplex.

nodes.label: No-signalling
nodes.desc: Marginal statistics of one party independent of the other party's setting.

nodes.label: Local tomography
nodes.desc: Composite states determined by local measurement statistics.

nodes.label: Purification
nodes.desc: Every mixed state is the marginal of a pure state, unique up to local reversible transformations (Chiribella-D'Ariano-Perinotti).

nodes.label: No-restriction hypothesis
nodes.desc: All mathematically well-defined effects (dual cone) are physical measurements.

nodes.label: Information causality
nodes.desc: m classical bits assisted by correlations transmit at most m bits of accessible information.

nodes.label: Macroscopic locality
nodes.desc: Coarse-grained correlations of many-particle experiments are classical.

nodes.label: Local orthogonality / exclusivity
nodes.desc: Sum of probabilities of pairwise exclusive events is at most 1 (Specker / E-principle).

nodes.label: No higher-order interference
nodes.desc: Sorkin hierarchy truncates at second order (pairwise slit interference only).

nodes.label: Decoherence to classical
nodes.desc: The theory contains a decoherence map onto a classical (simplicial) subtheory.

nodes.label: Classical probability (simplex)
nodes.desc: State space a simplex; effect cone its dual; the unique noncontextual, local, positive, broadcastable theory.

nodes.label: Quantum theory (complex)
nodes.desc: Density operators on complex Hilbert space; all POVMs; CP dynamics.

nodes.label: Real-amplitude QM
nodes.desc: Quantum theory over real Hilbert spaces with real tensor composites. Drops ax-complex; violates local tomography; falsified in network Bell tests.

nodes.label: Boxworld (GNST)
nodes.desc: Maximal no-signalling theory under no-restriction: square state spaces, PR boxes, trivial reversible dynamics.

nodes.label: Spekkens toy / epistricted theories
nodes.desc: Classical ontic states + knowledge-balance restriction (epistricted cluster, discrete case). Nonsimplicial but simplex-embeddable: nonclassical yet noncontextual.

nodes.label: Odd-d stabilizer subtheory
nodes.desc: Stabilizer states / Clifford / Pauli measurements, odd local dimension. Epistricted-cluster member: equals discrete epistricted mechanics (Gross Wigner).

nodes.label: Qubit (even-d) stabilizer subtheory
nodes.desc: Stabilizer states / Clifford / Pauli on qubits. The anomaly: NOT epistricted - state-independently contextual (Mermin square).

nodes.label: Gaussian quantum mechanics
nodes.desc: Gaussian states, Gaussian unitaries, quadrature measurements. Epistricted-cluster member: equals epistricted Liouville mechanics (Bartlett-Rudolph-Spekkens).

nodes.label: Separable quantum theory (min-tensor QM)
nodes.desc: Single systems fully quantum; composite cone = separable cone. Axiom: minimal tensor product; purification fails by construction.

nodes.label: Almost-quantum correlation set
nodes.desc: Correlation set Q(1+AB), slightly larger than quantum, satisfying most device-independent principles; incompatible with no-restriction.

nodes.label: psi-epistemic ontological models
nodes.desc: Ontological models in which distinct pure states have overlapping ontic distributions (Harrigan-Spekkens classification).

nodes.label: Separable states
nodes.desc: Convex mixtures of product states. LHV/LHS models exist by construction for all local measurements.

nodes.label: Entangled states
nodes.desc: States outside the separable cone of a composite.

nodes.label: Bound (PPT) entangled states
nodes.desc: Entangled but undistillable; positive partial transpose.

nodes.label: Basis-coherent states
nodes.desc: Off-diagonal terms w.r.t. a NAMED basis or fragment. Basis-relative by the spectral theorem (every rho is diagonal in its own eigenbasis), so every claim must name the basis. GPT counterpart: superposition / strong incompatibility.

nodes.label: Energy-coherent (non-TTS) states
nodes.desc: [rho, H] != 0: coherence across energy eigenspaces = asymmetry under time translations (unspeakable coherence).

nodes.label: TTS / energy-diagonal states
nodes.desc: [rho, H] = 0: time-translation symmetric states; block-diagonal in energy.

nodes.label: Thermal (Gibbs) states
nodes.desc: gamma = exp(-beta H)/Z; TTS, passive, full rank.

nodes.label: Athermal states
nodes.desc: Deviation from the Gibbs state; the free-energy resource of thermal operations (can be TTS: diagonal non-thermal populations).

nodes.label: Gaussian states
nodes.desc: Gaussian Wigner function: coherent, squeezed, thermal states of quadratic Hamiltonians.

nodes.label: Wigner-negative states
nodes.desc: Negativity of the (discrete or CV) Wigner function.

nodes.label: Stabilizer states
nodes.desc: Joint eigenstates (and mixtures) of Weyl/Pauli stabilizer groups; odd d: nonnegative Gross-Wigner function.

nodes.label: Magic (non-stabilizer) states
nodes.desc: States outside the stabilizer polytope; the injection resource for universal QC.

nodes.label: Discordant states
nodes.desc: Nonclassical correlations beyond entanglement (nonzero quantum discord).

nodes.label: Zero-discord (classical-classical) states
nodes.desc: Diagonal in a product basis; locally broadcastable; a strict subset of separable states.

nodes.label: Unitary / reversible dynamics
nodes.desc: U = exp(-iHt); via the complex structure, generators are observables (Stone / Noether link).

nodes.label: Clifford operations
nodes.desc: Normalizer of the Weyl/Pauli group; the free operations of stabilizer computation.

nodes.label: Gaussian operations
nodes.desc: Quadratic-Hamiltonian unitaries, Gaussian channels and homodyne measurements. Exactly the regime where Moyal = Poisson.

nodes.label: Non-Gaussian operations
nodes.desc: Cubic-or-higher generators; photon counting / parity measurements. Needed for CV universality and for generating Wigner negativity.

nodes.label: Covariant (TTS) processes
nodes.desc: Channels commuting with time translation: T(U_t rho U_t*) = U_t T(rho) U_t*. Cannot create asymmetry/energy coherence.

nodes.label: Thermal operations
nodes.desc: Energy-preserving unitaries with Gibbs ancillas; a subset of covariant and Gibbs-preserving maps.

nodes.label: Incoherent / dephasing-covariant ops
nodes.desc: Free operations of coherence resource theories: cannot create basis coherence.

nodes.label: LOCC / non-entangling ops
nodes.desc: Local operations + classical communication; free operations of entanglement theory: cannot create entanglement.

nodes.label: Local filters (SLOCC postselection)
nodes.desc: Probabilistic local maps; activate hidden nonlocality of LHV-modelable entangled states.

nodes.label: Projective energy measurement (TPM)
nodes.desc: Two-point projective scheme; the first measurement dephases all input energy coherence.

nodes.label: Weak / direct measurements + postselection
nodes.desc: Minimally invasive sequential probing; reads Kirkwood-Dirac values and weak values.

nodes.label: Sharp KS / Pauli measurement sets
nodes.desc: Fixed compatibility structures of sharp measurements: Pauli contexts (Mermin square), KS ray sets (KCBS, Yu-Oh).

nodes.label: Incompatible measurement sets
nodes.desc: No joint POVM reproducing all marginals; necessary resource on each wing for steering and Bell tests.

nodes.label: Bell / CHSH functional
nodes.desc: B = <A1B1>+<A1B2>+<A2B1>-<A2B2>. One functional, stratified thresholds: >2 Bell violation, 2*sqrt(2) Tsirelson (quantum max), 4 PR box. The recorded exception to strict 1-1 witness-effect pairing.

nodes.label: Steering inequality / LHS test
nodes.desc: Semidefinite membership test for local-hidden-state models of an assemblage {sigma_a|x}; violation of a steering inequality certifies steering.

nodes.label: Joint-measurability SDP
nodes.desc: SDP deciding whether a measurement set has a parent POVM; incompatibility robustness quantifies the margin.

nodes.label: Entanglement witness operator
nodes.desc: Hermitian W with Tr(W sigma) >= 0 for all separable sigma, Tr(W rho) < 0 for some entangled rho; complete by Hahn-Banach, but no efficient universal witness (separability NP-hard).

nodes.label: Noncontextuality inequalities / simplex-embedding LP
nodes.desc: Generalized-noncontextuality inequalities; the complete test is a linear program deciding simplex embeddability of the accessible GPT fragment.

nodes.label: State-independent KS sets
nodes.desc: Peres-Mermin square (2 qubits, 9 Paulis), Yu-Oh 13 rays (qutrit): the noncontextual bound is violated by EVERY state - maximally mixed and thermal included.

nodes.label: KCBS pentagon functional
nodes.desc: State-dependent KS functional: sum of 5 exclusive-projector probabilities <= 2 for NCHV; qutrit states reach sqrt(5) (Lovasz theta).

nodes.label: Displaced-parity (Wigner) estimator
nodes.desc: W(alpha) = (2/pi) Tr[rho D(alpha) Pi D(alpha)*] (CV); phase-point operators A_u (odd d). Measures the Wigner function point by point.

nodes.label: Kirkwood-Dirac distribution scheme
nodes.desc: Q(a,b) = Tr(Pi_a Pi_b rho), measured by weak-then-strong (direct) measurement; negativity or imaginarity is the nonclassicality flag.

nodes.label: Anomalous weak-value protocol
nodes.desc: A_w = <phi|A|psi>/<phi|psi> with postselection; anomalous when outside the spectrum of A; a conditioned KD expectation.

nodes.label: Work-quasiprobability protocol
nodes.desc: Weak-TPM interpolations / Margenau-Hill (real-KD) work distributions; negativity certifies contextuality of the work process.

nodes.label: Stabilizer / magic witnesses
nodes.desc: Robustness of magic, mana (log-negativity of the Gross-Wigner function, odd d), stabilizer fidelity and extent.

nodes.label: Coherence monotones / event-graph tests
nodes.desc: l1 and relative-entropy coherence monotones; interference visibility; event-graph (C_G) inequalities for basis-independent set coherence.

nodes.label: Local-broadcasting test
nodes.desc: rho_AB is locally broadcastable iff it has zero discord; operational failure of local broadcasting witnesses discord.

nodes.label: Cloning-fidelity bound
nodes.desc: Universal qubit cloner fidelity <= 5/6; the certified impossibility of exceeding it is the operational witness of no-broadcasting.

nodes.label: Fringe visibility
nodes.desc: Two-path visibility V with duality V^2 + D^2 <= 1. Caveat recorded as D3: visibility alone does NOT certify nonclassicality (epistricted theories reproduce it).

nodes.label: Sorkin I3 estimator
nodes.desc: I3 = P123 - P12 - P13 - P23 + P1 + P2 + P3. Identically zero in quantum theory: a null test that fires only in beyond-quantum (density-cube) theories.

nodes.label: Bell inequality violation
nodes.desc: No local-hidden-variable model for space-like separated statistics.

nodes.label: EPR steering
nodes.desc: No local-hidden-state model for an assemblage.

nodes.label: Measurement incompatibility
nodes.desc: No joint measurement reproducing the marginals.

nodes.label: KS contextuality (state-independent)
nodes.desc: No outcome-deterministic noncontextual value assignment to sharp measurements.

nodes.label: State-dependent KS contextuality
nodes.desc: Violation of a KS-type noncontextuality inequality by a specific state (e.g. KCBS).

nodes.label: Generalized (Spekkens) contextuality
nodes.desc: No generalized-noncontextual ontological model; GPT form: failure of simplex embeddability.

nodes.label: No-cloning / no-broadcasting
nodes.desc: Impossibility of a map broadcasting all states.

nodes.label: Second-order interference
nodes.desc: Two-path interference phenomenology (fringes, Elitzur-Vaidman, delayed choice).

nodes.label: Higher-order interference
nodes.desc: Nonzero Sorkin third-or-higher-order interference terms.

nodes.label: Anomalous weak values
nodes.desc: Weak values outside the eigenvalue range.

nodes.label: Kirkwood-Dirac nonpositivity
nodes.desc: Negativity or imaginarity of the KD quasiprobability of an experiment.

nodes.label: Anomalous work / heat flows
nodes.desc: Work or heat statistics impossible for noncontextual / classically correlated processes.

nodes.label: Superquantum (PR) correlations
nodes.desc: No-signalling correlations beyond the Tsirelson bound.

nodes.label: DI randomness & QKD
nodes.desc: Device-independent certification from Bell violation.

nodes.label: One-sided DI QKD
nodes.desc: Security from steering with one untrusted party.

nodes.label: BB84 key distribution
nodes.desc: Prepare-measure key distribution.

nodes.label: Parity-oblivious multiplexing / RAC
nodes.desc: Communication games bounded by preparation noncontextuality.

nodes.label: Universal QC (state injection / MBQC)
nodes.desc: Promoting free (stabilizer / Clifford) operations to universality.

nodes.label: State-discrimination advantage
nodes.desc: Minimum-error discrimination beyond noncontextual bounds.

nodes.label: Postselected metrology
nodes.desc: Fisher-information advantages from quasiprobability negativity.

nodes.label: Entanglement witnessing / separability
nodes.desc: Detecting entanglement; complexity of deciding separability.

nodes.label: Deciding the quantum set
nodes.desc: Complexity/decidability of membership in quantum correlations.

nodes.label: Second laws / work extraction
nodes.desc: State conversion under thermal operations; work from coherence and correlations.

nodes.label: QRT axioms (F, O)
nodes.desc: A quantum resource theory is a pair (F, O): free states F and free operations O with the golden rule O(F) subset of F. The maximal class is RNG (resource non-generating). Theories are classified by how O is justified physically.

nodes.label: Convexity axiom
nodes.desc: F convex and closed. Then every resource state is separated from F by a hyperplane: witnesses exist, and the generalized robustness R(rho) = min{s : (rho + s sigma)/(1+s) in F} is well defined.

nodes.label: Tensor / monoidal axiom
nodes.desc: F closed under tensor products and partial trace (symmetric monoidal structure of Coecke-Fritz-Spekkens). Prerequisite for asymptotic (many-copy) rates.

nodes.label: Generalized Stein lemma / second law
nodes.desc: For F satisfying the Brandao-Plenio axioms, the Stein exponent of resource testing equals the regularized relative entropy of resource; consequence: asymptotic reversibility under asymptotically resource-non-generating operations, with the regularized relativ…

nodes.label: Universal operational advantage
nodes.desc: In any convex QRT, every resource state strictly outperforms all free states in some (sub)channel discrimination task, and the generalized robustness is the exact maximal advantage. Extended beyond convexity via multi-copy discrimination.

nodes.label: QP1: typology of free operations
nodes.desc: DERIVED classification. The 12 proper theories split by the physical justification of O: symmetry-type (asymmetry; unspeakable coherence; imaginarity as antiunitary Z2 analogue), subtheory-type (magic, CV non-Gaussianity), partition-type (entanglement, steeri…

nodes.label: LQICC / LICC (ENT x COH)
nodes.desc: Intersection classes (local quantum-incoherent operations and classical communication): the arena in which entanglement and coherence are interconverted and assisted-distilled.

nodes.label: Catalysis
nodes.desc: Catalysts enlarge the reachable set in many theories: entanglement catalysis (Jonathan-Plenio), catalytic coherence (Aberg), catalytic thermodynamics; a cross-theory phenomenon of the operations layer and a candidate route around exact-RNG irreversibility (en…

nodes.label: Maximal (RNG) classes
nodes.desc: NE (entanglement), MIO (coherence), GPO (athermality), CSPO-type (magic), covariant (asymmetry), unital (purity). Reversibility statements live here and are class-sensitive: exact vs asymptotic non-generation is the load-bearing distinction.

nodes.label: Witness existence (Hahn-Banach)
nodes.desc: Convexity + closedness of F implies every resource state is detected by some linear witness. The convexity axiom translated to the witness layer.

nodes.label: Robustness = discrimination advantage
nodes.desc: Generalized robustness is exactly the maximal advantage of a resource state over all free states in a class of subchannel discrimination tasks - one witness/task pair that every convex theory instantiates.

nodes.label: Channel discrimination (universal task)
nodes.desc: The universal task: every resource of every convex theory buys a strict advantage here; steering's version is subchannel discrimination with 1W-LOCC measurements.

nodes.label: Constraint: no purity source
nodes.desc: Constraint-type model: the only free state is the maximally mixed one; free ops = noisy operations; state pre-order = majorization; equivalent to athermality with trivial Hamiltonian.

nodes.label: Gibbs constraint x U(1) covariance
nodes.desc: Constraint x symmetry type: energy conservation (U(1)-covariance of TO) + unique full-rank fixed point gamma (Gibbs preservation). Block-diagonal sector governed by thermomajorization; coherent sector by asymmetry theory. The unique two-axiom intersection of…

nodes.label: G-covariance (reference frames)
nodes.desc: Symmetry-type: group G acts by a unitary representation; free = invariant states; O = covariant channels. Monotone set strictly larger than speakable-coherence monotone set.

nodes.label: Dephasing-defined (basis-relative)
nodes.desc: F = fixed points of the dephasing map Delta. Free-op zoo MIO > {IO, DIO} > SIO reflects the absence of a single physical justification (Marvian-Spekkens critique); TIO < DIO is the symmetry-justified subclass.

nodes.label: Antiunitary Z2 (conjugation)
nodes.desc: Z2 analogue of coherence with respect to an ANTIUNITARY (complex conjugation K): free = K-invariant states. Not a G-covariance theory in the usual sense because K is not a channel; free ops defined by real Kraus operators.

nodes.label: Stabilizer subtheory (Gottesman-Knill)
nodes.desc: Subtheory-type: the stabilizer subtheory is classically simulable; resource = whatever lies outside its convex hull. Odd d: distillation-relevant boundary characterized by discrete-Wigner positivity.

nodes.label: Gaussian subtheory (CV)
nodes.desc: Subtheory-type CV twin of magic: Gaussian subtheory simulable; Wigner negativity is the resource for CV quantum-computational advantage (positive Wigner implies efficient classical simulation).

nodes.label: LOCC partition (two labs)
nodes.desc: Partition-type: spatially separated labs; O = LOCC (classical communication allowed). Maximal class NE (non-entangling).

nodes.label: One-sided trust (1W-LOCC)
nodes.desc: Partition-type with asymmetric trust: one characterized (trusted) and one uncharacterized wing; O = one-way LOCC from the trusted wing.

nodes.label: Common cause, no communication
nodes.desc: Partition-type with no communication: resources are common-cause boxes; O = the polytope of LOSR wirings; classical/nonclassical defined by the causal model required.

nodes.label: Compatibility structures (NCW)
nodes.desc: Partition-type over compatibility structures: behaviors on measurement scenarios; O = noncontextual wirings; unifies KS contextuality and Bell nonlocality in one framework.

nodes.label: Device programmability
nodes.desc: Resource on measurement DEVICES, not states: incompatibility = quantum programmability of a classical-output device; complete convertibility conditions via discrimination with post-measurement information. Shows the QRT schema extends to dynamical objects.

nodes.label: Fails convexity + golden rule
nodes.desc: FAILS two framework axioms: (i) the classical-state set is non-convex; (ii) local channels can create discord, so no golden-rule free-op class contains even local processing. Discord quantities remain meaningful but discord is not a QRT in the standard sense.

nodes.label: I/d (unique free state)
nodes.desc: The free set is the single state I/d - the smallest free set in the compilation, making purity the bottom currency: every other theory's free set contains it.

nodes.label: Nonuniform states
nodes.desc: Any rho != I/d is a resource. Pre-order: majorization (complete); asymptotic rate log d - S(rho); fully reversible with no bound resources - the benchmark reversible theory.

nodes.label: Gibbs state gamma (unique)
nodes.desc: Unique free state e^{-beta H}/Z: the only state that is both a fixed point of the Gibbs constraint AND U(1)-symmetric - the state-level shadow of the two-axiom intersection (QP1).

nodes.label: Athermal states
nodes.desc: Any rho != gamma. Block-diagonal sector ordered by thermomajorization; coherent sector constrained independently by asymmetry modes (neither family alone complete).

nodes.label: Symmetric (G-invariant) states
nodes.desc: U_g rho U_g^dag = rho for all g. For U(1) generated by H with nondegenerate spectrum: exactly the energy-incoherent states.

nodes.label: Asymmetric states (clocks/frames)
nodes.desc: [rho, H] != 0 for translations: unspeakable coherence. Quantified by the QFI family; pure-state asymmetry not captured by any single entropic measure.

nodes.label: Incoherent (diagonal) states
nodes.desc: Diagonal in the fixed reference basis: Delta(rho) = rho.

nodes.label: Coherent states
nodes.desc: Off-diagonal in the fixed basis; golden unit |+_d>. Every coherent state is distillable at rate C_r under IO - no bound coherence exists.

nodes.label: Real states
nodes.desc: Density matrices with real entries in the fixed basis (invariant under conjugation K).

nodes.label: Imaginary states
nodes.desc: States with nonzero imaginary parts; golden unit (|0> + i|1>)/sqrt(2); qubit and pure-state conversion fully solved.

nodes.label: STAB (stabilizer polytope)
nodes.desc: Convex hull of stabilizer states; classically simulable (Gottesman-Knill). Contains maximally entangled states (Bell, GHZ): free-of-magic is not free-of-entanglement.

nodes.label: Magic (non-stabilizer) states
nodes.desc: Outside STAB; golden unit T state. Odd d: mana > 0 iff discrete-Wigner-negative; Wigner-positive non-stabilizer states are BOUND magic (undistillable).

nodes.label: Wigner-positive states
nodes.desc: Nonnegative CV Wigner function (resp. convex hull of Gaussians); positive-Wigner dynamics is classically simulable.

nodes.label: Wigner-negative states
nodes.desc: Negativity of the CV Wigner function; golden unit Fock |1>; necessary for CV computational advantage and equivalent to CV contextuality.

nodes.label: SEP (separable states)
nodes.desc: Convex mixtures of product states. Deciding membership is NP-hard; witnesses complete by Hahn-Banach.

nodes.label: Entangled states
nodes.desc: Outside SEP; golden unit ebit |Phi+>. E_D < E_C in general: bound entangled (PPT) states have E_D = 0 < E_C.

nodes.label: LHS (unsteerable) assemblages
nodes.desc: Assemblages admitting local-hidden-state models. Strictly between the neighbors: SEP < unsteerable < Bell-local, both inclusions strict (Werner ranges).

nodes.label: Steerable assemblages
nodes.desc: No LHS model. Steering requires BOTH entanglement of the state and incompatibility of the untrusted measurements, jointly.

nodes.label: Local (classical-cause) boxes
nodes.desc: Common-cause boxes explained by a classical causal model. Caveat QP2: the STATE-level Bell-local set is not tensor-stable (superactivation); boxes under LOSR, not states, are the proper free objects.

nodes.label: Nonlocal boxes
nodes.desc: Boxes violating some Bell inequality; every convexly extremal quantumly realizable box is at the top of the quantum LOSR pre-order; the PR box is the beyond-quantum top.

nodes.label: Noncontextual behaviors
nodes.desc: Behaviors with noncontextual models on the scenario's compatibility structure. Bell-local behaviors are the special case where contexts are spacelike (SS15).

nodes.label: Contextual behaviors
nodes.desc: Violate some noncontextuality inequality; maximally contextual boxes ('contextuality bits') exist for broad scenario classes.

nodes.label: Jointly measurable sets
nodes.desc: POVM collections with a parent measurement - equivalently, devices programmable with classical programs.

nodes.label: Incompatible sets
nodes.desc: No parent POVM. In one-to-one correspondence with steerable assemblages (SS10); golden unit: mutually unbiased sharp pair.

nodes.label: Classical-classical states
nodes.desc: Diagonal in a product basis; locally broadcastable. The set is NON-CONVEX: mixing CC states of different bases is discordant - the convexity-axiom violation (MM9).

nodes.label: Discordant states
nodes.desc: Any state not classical-classical, separable states included. Relative entropy of quantumness = minimal distillable entanglement generated by the activation protocol.

nodes.label: I/d - shared bottom
nodes.desc: Member of every free set considered here EXCEPT purity, where it is the unique free state, and athermality, where it is free only at infinite temperature (trivial H). The universal bottom of all pre-orders.

nodes.label: Gibbs gamma - thermal magic
nodes.desc: Unique athermality-free state; incoherent in the energy basis (nondegenerate H); U(1)-symmetric; real in the energy basis; separable for noninteracting local H. But for a generic interacting H, gamma is NOT a stabilizer state: the thermal state of one theory…

nodes.label: |+> - coherent yet magic-free
nodes.desc: Stabilizer and real and pure: free in magic and imaginarity, maximal resource in coherence (basis Z), purity, and U(1)-asymmetry (H prop Z). Witnesses that coherence is NOT sufficient for magic.

nodes.label: T state - four-theory resource
nodes.desc: (|0> + e^{i pi/4}|1>)/sqrt(2): simultaneously a resource of magic, coherence, purity AND imaginarity; injection yields the T gate and universality.

nodes.label: Wigner-positive magic (bound)
nodes.desc: Odd d: states outside STAB yet with mana = 0; useless for magic distillation and classically simulable - the magic analogue of bound entanglement.

nodes.label: Bell |Phi+> - entangled, magic-free
nodes.desc: Maximally entangled, maximally steering-capable, Bell-violating (with incompatible measurements) - yet a stabilizer state (magic-free) and real (imaginarity-free). Shows STAB is not inside SEP: free sets of different theories cut across each other.

nodes.label: Werner states - strictness witness
nodes.desc: Entangled for p > 1/3; admit LHV models for projective measurements in a range (Werner) and even for POVMs (Barrett); unsteerable range (WJD). The canonical witness that SEP < unsteerable < Bell-local is strict.

nodes.label: Bound entangled states
nodes.desc: PPT entangled: E_D = 0 < E_C. Some bound entangled states violate Bell inequalities (Peres conjecture false): nonlocality without distillability.

nodes.label: Discordant separable states
nodes.desc: Separable (entanglement-free) yet discordant; the input class for discord-to-entanglement activation.

nodes.label: Noisy / unital operations
nodes.desc: Noisy operations (unitaries + maximally mixed ancillas + partial trace); unital maps give the same single-system state pre-order (majorization).

nodes.label: Work from purity; coherence prep
nodes.desc: Purity as fuel: kT ln2 of work per pure bit (Landauer/Szilard); and via free unitaries it converts into maximal coherence in any chosen basis, which bounds downstream entanglement and discord generation (QP4 cascade).

nodes.label: Thermal operations (TO)
nodes.desc: Energy-conserving unitaries + Gibbs ancillas: Gibbs-preserving AND U(1)-covariant. Strictly inside GPO: a Gibbs-preserving map can create energy coherence while TO cannot. Whether TO = GPO intersect TIO exactly is open here (QG2).

nodes.label: Work extraction & conversion
nodes.desc: Spending athermality: single-shot deterministic work set by min-free-energy; the F_alpha second laws govern which conversions TO can perform; correlations (incl. entanglement) carry extra extractable work beyond the marginals.

nodes.label: No coherence distillation; work locking
nodes.desc: Impossible even with resources: coherence distillation machines do not exist - under thermal/covariant processing the distillable coherence of every full-rank state is ZERO even with unlimited work, while the coherence cost equals the QFI; and work stored in…

nodes.label: G-covariant channels
nodes.desc: Channels commuting with the group action. For U(1) time translations: TIO, strictly inside DIO (group averaging implements dephasing covariance).

nodes.label: Metrology, clocks, catalytic use
nodes.desc: Spending asymmetry: phase-estimation precision = QFI (an asymmetry monotone); clock synchronization and reference-frame alignment consume it; catalytic coherence (Aberg) permits repeated use of one coherent battery.

nodes.label: Incoherent-op lattice (MIO...SIO)
nodes.desc: SIO subset of IO and DIO; IO, DIO subset of MIO; TIO subset of DIO; IO and DIO incomparable. MIO = maximal (RNG) class.

nodes.label: Distillation & dilution (IO)
nodes.desc: Spending coherence: every coherent state distills |+> at rate C_r under IO; dilution from |+> costs C_f; coherent inputs power what incoherent ones cannot - e.g. entanglement generation via bipartite IO (C1).

nodes.label: No reversible IO cycle (mixed)
nodes.desc: Impossible even with resources: under IO, C_f > C_r for generic mixed states, so distill-then-dilute cannot return the input at par. Reversibility holds only under asymptotically resource-non-generating (MIO-type) operations at rate C_r (Stein-lemma regime).

nodes.label: Real operations (real Kraus)
nodes.desc: Channels with real Kraus operators; local real ops + classical communication (LRCC) define the distributed theory.

nodes.label: Local discrimination with i
nodes.desc: Spending imaginarity: real orthogonal pure-state pairs that LOCC distinguishes perfectly become indistinguishable (no better than guessing in the worst case) when one party is restricted to real operations - the imaginary resource buys the gap.

nodes.label: Stabilizer ops / CSPO
nodes.desc: Stabilizer protocols (Clifford unitaries, Pauli measurements, stabilizer ancillas, feed-forward) subset of completely stabilizer-preserving operations (channel-maximal class for simulation bounds).

nodes.label: State injection -> universality
nodes.desc: Spending magic: T-state injection promotes stabilizer circuits to universal quantum computation; robustness of magic prices the classical-simulation overhead of the spent states.

nodes.label: Bound magic; no unit-rate cycle
nodes.desc: Impossible even with resources: Wigner-positive magic states cannot be distilled by stabilizer operations (bound magic); and equal-mana state classes exist that do NOT interconvert at unit rate - magic is asymptotically irreversible under STAB ops.

nodes.label: Gaussian protocols
nodes.desc: Gaussian unitaries, Gaussian measurements, feed-forward; cannot create Wigner negativity.

nodes.label: Negativity -> CV advantage
nodes.desc: Spending Wigner negativity: injected into Gaussian circuits it lifts them beyond efficient classical simulation - the CV analogue of magic injection.

nodes.label: LOCC (< SEP < PPT < NE)
nodes.desc: Local operations + classical communication; the ladder continues upward through separable, PPT-preserving and non-entangling operations, each step changing which states count as equivalent.

nodes.label: Teleportation, dense coding, distillation
nodes.desc: Spending ebits: teleportation and dense coding consume maximal entanglement; distillation protocols concentrate noisy entanglement; every entangled state wins some semiquantum game (Buscemi) - a measurement-device-independent certificate that all entanglement…

nodes.label: No second law (exact NE); bound ENT
nodes.desc: Impossible even with resources: under EXACTLY non-entangling operations, entanglement manipulation is asymptotically irreversible - no single measure governs all transformations, so no axiomatic second law; and bound entangled states cannot be distilled by LO…

nodes.label: One-way LOCC (trusted -> untrusted)
nodes.desc: Local ops + one-way classical communication from the trusted party: the free operations that cannot create steering.

nodes.label: 1sDI QKD; subchannel discrimination
nodes.desc: Spending steering: one-sided device-independent key distribution is secured exactly by steerability; steering = advantage in subchannel discrimination restricted to 1W-LOCC measurements (Piani-Watrous).

nodes.label: LOSR wirings (polytope)
nodes.desc: The free operations on common-cause boxes form a polytope; convertibility between boxes is decidable by linear programming.

nodes.label: DI certification; superactivation
nodes.desc: Spending nonlocality: Bell violation certifies device-independent keys and randomness; and tensoring + local measurements SUPERACTIVATES hidden nonlocality - k copies of some Bell-local entangled states jointly violate a Bell inequality (Palazuelos).

nodes.label: Noncontextual wirings (NCW)
nodes.desc: Explicit parametrized class of contextuality-free operations on behaviors; forms a convex set; restricted to Bell scenarios NCW is NOT the same operation set as LOSR (P6).

nodes.label: POM / RAC advantage
nodes.desc: Spending contextuality: preparation contextuality powers parity-oblivious multiplexing beyond any noncontextual bound; contextual fraction quantifies the advantage.

nodes.label: Pre- + classical post-processing
nodes.desc: Compatibility-non-decreasing maps on devices: quantum pre-processing by a channel + classical post-processing of outcomes.

nodes.label: Discrimination with PMI
nodes.desc: Spending incompatibility: every incompatible set strictly beats all compatible ones in some state-discrimination game with post-measurement information; the game family is COMPLETE for the convertibility pre-order.

nodes.label: No free-op class exists
nodes.desc: Golden-rule failure: a local channel acting on one share of a classical-classical state can CREATE discord, so no free-operation class containing even local processing exists - the operations-layer pathology that disqualifies discord as a standard QRT.

nodes.label: Activation protocol (CNOT)
nodes.desc: Spending discord: local CNOT interactions with ancillas map any discordant state (separable included) to one with distillable system-ancilla entanglement; REQ = the minimal entanglement so generated. Also: discord = minimal entanglement created between system…

nodes.label: Purity detectors
nodes.desc: Tr rho^2 > 1/d, or any measurement statistics deviating from uniform - the simplest witness in the compilation.

nodes.label: Nonuniformity monotones
nodes.desc: log d - S(rho) and the Renyi nonuniformity family; majorization is a COMPLETE monotone family - detection and quantification coincide here.

nodes.label: Athermality witnesses
nodes.desc: Deviation from Gibbs statistics; operationally, any positive extractable work certifies athermality.

nodes.label: Second laws F_alpha + modes
nodes.desc: The Renyi free energies F_alpha (complete on block-diagonal states) PLUS the asymmetry-mode monotones for coherences: two families, jointly complete, separately incomplete - the witness-level image of the two-axiom model (QP1).

nodes.label: Covariance tests
nodes.desc: Any noninvariance of outcome statistics under the group action; mode-resolved tomography detects which asymmetry modes are populated.

nodes.label: QFI family; speed limits
nodes.desc: Quantum Fisher information is an asymmetry monotone; Mandelstam-Tamm and Margolus-Levitin speed limits are asymmetry bounds; under thermal covariant processing QFI is exactly the coherence COST.

nodes.label: Interferometric witnesses
nodes.desc: Robustness of coherence is directly measurable via witness-based lower bounds and interferometric visibility.

nodes.label: C_r, C_f, l1, robustness
nodes.desc: Relative entropy of coherence C_r (= distillable), coherence of formation C_f (= cost), l1-norm, robustness (= discrimination advantage, W2 instance).

nodes.label: LOCC vs real-LOCC gap
nodes.desc: Operational witness: the discrimination gap that appears when one party is restricted to real operations; realized in optical experiments.

nodes.label: Imaginarity monotones
nodes.desc: Robustness of imaginarity and geometric imaginarity; pure-state and qubit conversion fully characterized by them.

nodes.label: Magic witnesses
nodes.desc: Mana > 0 (odd d), robustness > 1, stabilizer-fidelity thresholds: each certifies nonstabilizerness.

nodes.label: Mana; robustness of magic
nodes.desc: Mana (additive, odd d), robustness of magic (prices classical-simulation overhead), stabilizer extent - quantifiers tied to distillation and simulation bounds.

nodes.label: Negativity estimators
nodes.desc: Displaced-parity measurements reconstruct W(alpha) point by point; any measured negative value certifies the resource.

nodes.label: Wigner log-negativity
nodes.desc: Monotone under Gaussian protocols; bounds the cost of classical simulation of CV circuits.

nodes.label: Entanglement witnesses; PPT
nodes.desc: Linear witnesses are complete for the convex SEP set (Hahn-Banach); PPT is a one-sided criterion; deciding separability is NP-hard.

nodes.label: E_D, E_C, E_r, negativity
nodes.desc: Distillable entanglement, entanglement cost, relative entropy of entanglement, negativity, robustness. The E_D < E_C gap on bound states is the single-shot face of the irreversibility formalized in pX-ent.

nodes.label: Steering inequalities; LHS-SDP
nodes.desc: SDP membership tests for LHS models; steering inequalities import one-to-one from joint-measurability (incompatibility) criteria.

nodes.label: Steering robustness & weight
nodes.desc: Steering robustness equals the advantage in subchannel discrimination with 1W-LOCC measurements - the steering instance of the universal robustness theorem.

nodes.label: Bell inequalities (detect only)
nodes.desc: Facet Bell-inequality violations certify nonclassicality of the common cause.

nodes.label: LOSR monotones (quantify)
nodes.desc: The information in the degrees of violation of ALL facet Bell inequalities does NOT determine the LOSR pre-order: quantification strictly exceeds witnessing in this theory.

nodes.label: Noncontextuality inequalities
nodes.desc: Scenario inequalities; the contextual fraction detects and grades violation.

nodes.label: Rel. entropy of contextuality
nodes.desc: An NCW-monotone (the completeness question for a monotone family under NCW is open territory, cf. QG3).

nodes.label: Incompatibility witnesses
nodes.desc: Detection via steering (SS10), via noise robustness thresholds, and via discrimination advantages.

nodes.label: Guessing-game family (complete)
nodes.desc: State discrimination with post-measurement information yields a COMPLETE monotone family: it decides convertibility of programmable devices, not just detection.

nodes.label: Local-broadcasting test
nodes.desc: A state is locally broadcastable iff it has zero discord; operational failure of local broadcasting witnesses discord.

nodes.label: Discord; REQ
nodes.desc: Quantum discord; relative entropy of quantumness = minimal distillable entanglement generated by activation - a quantifier with an entanglement-denominated operational meaning.

nodes.label: Order of magnitude
nodes.desc: Rounds a value to the nearest power of ten so that very different scales can be compared multiplicatively.

nodes.label: SI system of units
nodes.desc: The convention that fixes base quantities and their units and builds every other unit as a product of powers of them.

nodes.label: Time
nodes.desc: Read from a clock. SI unit the second, fixed by the caesium-133 hyperfine transition frequency.

nodes.label: Length
nodes.desc: Read from a ruler. SI unit the metre, fixed by the distance light travels in vacuum in 1/299 792 458 s.

nodes.label: Mass
nodes.desc: Inertial measure of the amount of matter, read from a balance. SI unit the kilogram, fixed since 2019 through Planck's constant.

nodes.label: Unit conversion
nodes.desc: Multiplies a quantity by a ratio equal to one, so the number changes and the quantity does not.

nodes.label: Dimensional analysis
nodes.desc: Tracks the powers of base dimensions in a quantity; an equation is admissible only if both sides carry the same dimension.

nodes.label: Estimation (Fermi)
nodes.desc: Obtains an order-of-magnitude answer from rough inputs combined in a dimensionally consistent way.

nodes.label: Discrepancy
nodes.desc: Difference between a measured value and the accepted value; a small discrepancy means high accuracy.

nodes.label: Uncertainty
nodes.desc: The spread of a measured value; percent uncertainty δA/A·100 % compares it with the value itself. Small spread means high precision.

nodes.label: Uncertainty propagation
